meta.disclaimer: Seed catalog for a new-car buying aid, not a certified data source. Figures come from manufacturer WLTP/spec sheets and third-party charging-curve databases and have not all been cross-checked per car against one primary source; cars flagged with a notes field below need that check before go-live. The original 15 entries (12.09.2026) implied a WLTP consumption (usableKwh / wltpKm) below the 15-20 kWh/100 km band typical for these vehicle classes, ranging 10.4-14.7 kWh/100 km - this may mean published WLTP ranges were sourced against gross (not usable) battery capacity, or that several wltpKm values are optimistic; do not treat wltpKm as an independent cross-check on usableKwh until each car's gross-capacity figure is recorded too. The 15 entries added 13.09.2026 to widen the catalog's price and body-style spread deliberately push that band open at the top end: most sit inside the original 10.4-14.7 kWh/100 km pattern, but the largest/heaviest additions (mercedes-g580 ~22.8, vw-id-buzz ~18.7, toyota-bz4x ~17.4 kWh/100 km implied) sit well above it on purpose - these are the catalog's intentional 'big battery, still weak on the Autobahn' examples, not data errors (see each car's notes). A second expansion later the same day added 28 more cars, taking the catalog from 33 to 61, so that every body style has a real field behind it (hatch 12, compact 7, kombi 7, sedan 9, crossover 26) and the price axis is populated end to end rather than at its extremes: the 28 span 18.900 to 84.100 EUR, including several cars that are deliberately poor on a long trip (leapmotor-t03 at 48 kW peak, mg5-kombi at 87 kW, opel-frontera at 305 km WLTP) and several that are deliberately strong (mercedes-cla-sb, audi-a6-etron, hyundai-ioniq6), because a comparison in which every car is adequate answers nothing. Every car's highwayKwhPer100 still clearly exceeds its own implied WLTP figure, old and new alike; for the 28 the implied-to-highway factor was checked to sit inside 1.24-1.57, which is the band the existing catalog already occupied.
meta.confidence: seed - unverified overall; nothing here has been cross-checked against a primary source. 52 of 61 cars carry a `notes` field: the original 4 (tesla-m3, tesla-my, mercedes-eqa, renault-5, flagged 12.09.2026) each mark one specific suspect figure, while the 15 cars added earlier on 13.09.2026 and all 28 added in the second expansion the same day are marked unverified in full, since none of their fields were checked against a manufacturer source at all. The remaining 9 cars (vw-id3, vw-id7, skoda-elroq, kia-ev3, bmw-ix1, volvo-ex30, byd-dolphin, byd-seal, opel-corsa) carry no notes field and were not re-examined - absence of a note is not a claim of verification. Two figures in the second expansion were changed after entry for internal consistency rather than from a source: vw-id4 and skoda-enyaq were moved from 135 to 175 kW peak to match skoda-elroq, with which they share the MEB 77 kWh pack; if that assumption is wrong, three charging-curve entries are wrong with it. See lib/engine/charge.ts for the related AVG_KW_10_80 flags: the 12.09.2026 finding on skoda-elroq and kia-ev3 (both confirmed conservative) is unchanged, and the second expansion adds 13 entries derived from platform siblings already in that table while leaving 15 of the 28 new cars on the plain peak-based fallback, for lack of any specific figure to reason from. Derived-from-a-sibling is not sourced: if a sibling's figure is corrected, every entry that was copied from it must be corrected too.
